summary: Merve Noyan (Hugging Face open-source team) frames the talk as having an AI engineer at your fingertips. She argues open-source ML is now differentially advantageous: open weights allow shrinking, quantization, fine-tuning, and private edge/browser deployment, with no silent performance degradation. GLM 5.1 tops the Artificial Analysis intelligence index, with open models catching up to closed ones. Hugging Face Hub (~3M models, datasets, spaces) is the infra layer. Agentic models increasingly ship day-zero with vision capabilities (Gemini omni, Qwen 3.5, Chimera 2.5); vision LLMs can act as computer-use agents over screenshots. New Hub features include benchmark datasets (SWE-bench Pro, Humanity's Last Exam, AIME) for ranking models by score, and inference providers (Groq, Cerebras, Novita) that route by cheapest/fastest option with tool-use columns. The Hub ships an MCP server exposing models, datasets, spaces (described as the App Store of AI), and jobs (one-off paid-by-duration compute jobs). MCP can query remote Spaces dynamically; a demo generates an image of 'baklava made of yarn' via Qwen image Space, requiring an experimental 'dynamic spaces' setting for full access. Hermes agent is highlighted for superior memory management and Slack/WhatsApp integration; GLM 5.1 autonomously fixed a Slack integration bug. A new 'traces' dataset repository type stores, parses, and visualizes agent sessions and supports training on those traces. Practical serving tips: use the Hub's 'Other > apps' tab for local-serving tools, check GGUF sections for hardware compatibility (Gemma 4-bit fits an L4 24GB GPU), and use the 'Use this model' button for serving commands. HF skills include HF CLI, LLM trainer, Gradio, dataset, and a new OCR recommendation skill. A live demo shows Claude Code fine-tuning Qwen-2-VL on Llava-Instruct-Mix with automated VRAM calculation and remote job launch. Skills extend to vision tasks (object detection, segmentation with bounding box types). A case study by colleague Niels OCR'd 30,000 AI papers using Codex open OCR models and jobs entirely through prompting: pick an OCR model via OCR-bench, ask the LLM to write and launch the processing job, and the skill handles instance setup. A new skill recommends best OCR models for fine-tuning. HF's new 'buckets' infra product (cheaper and faster than S3) supports job reruns via mounting.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction & Open Source Importance
sections.summary: Merve introduces the talk as having an AI engineer at your fingertips. She distinguishes open weights (non-commercial) from open source (commercially licensed like MIT/Apache 2.0) and fully open (code + harness open). Open weights enable quantization, fine-tuning, and private edge deployment; no silent performance degradation. GLM 5.1 leads the Artificial Analysis index, with open models catching up to closed ones.

sections.title: Hugging Face Hub & Agentic/Vision Models
sections.summary: Hub (~3M models, datasets, spaces) is the infra layer for open-source workflows. Agentic models trending on Hub split into LLMs and vision LLMs; VLMs can act as computer-use agents over screenshots. Trend: labs release LLMs day-zero with vision (Gemini omni, Qwen 3.5, Chimera 2.5). Running via VLLM, MLX, or llama.cpp is now low-friction.

sections.title: Benchmark Datasets & Model Filtering
sections.summary: New benchmark datasets feature: click 'benchmark' on datasets to see SWE-bench Pro, Humanity's Last Exam, AIME, etc. SWE-bench ranks open models by coding scores; GLM 5.1 tops the list. Makes selecting among 3M models tractable.

sections.title: Inference Providers & Model Routing
sections.summary: HF inference providers route requests to best providers (Groq, Cerebras, Novita). UI shows cheapest and fastest options plus a tool-use column for agentic use cases, enabling easy model comparison.

sections.title: Local Coding Agents & Tools
sections.summary: Hub ships MCP server, skills, and local agent integrations. 'pie' is a favorite local coding agent; can use inference providers or llama.cpp locally. llama.cpp includes an embedded agent binary that starts a model given an HF Hub ID.

sections.title: Hermes Agent for Memory Management
sections.summary: Hermes agent offers superior memory management beyond open-claw. Setup wizard handles keys and Slack/WhatsApp integration. Speaker recommends pairing with GLM 5.1, which autonomously fixed a Slack integration bug. Looks forward to using it with Gemma 4 and rumored Minimax model.

sections.title: Traces Repository for Agent Sessions
sections.summary: New 'traces' dataset repository type hosts Codex, Claude Code, or pie traces. Dataset viewer parses traces nicely; you can later train a model on them. Upload sessions from specified paths - no extra steps. Hermes agent traces support coming soon.

sections.title: Tips for Finding & Serving Local Models
sections.summary: Use the Hub's 'Other > apps' tab to filter models supported by LM Studio, llama.cpp, etc. GGUF section on model pages shows hardware compatibility (e.g., Gemma 4-bit fits L4 24GB GPU). 'Use this model' button gives ready-to-run serving commands for local apps.

sections.title: Supercharging Agents with HF Skills
sections.summary: HF skills include HF CLI (manage repos, run jobs, launch demos), LLM trainer (remote/local training for LLMs and VLMs), Gradio (build demos), and dataset (explore via dataset viewer API). Integrations with Claude Code and Gemini. Install via 'HF skills' Google search.

sections.title: Live Demo & Vision Model Training
sections.summary: Live demo: Claude Code asked to train Qwen-2-VL on Llava-Instruct-Mix. Agent asks clarifying questions (instance, validation split), calculates VRAM in background, and launches remote job. Final model appears on the Hub. Skills also support vision tasks like object detection and segmentation. Teases MCP coverage in second half.

sections.title: MCP Server: Spaces, Jobs & Dynamic Spaces
sections.summary: MCP serves models, datasets, spaces, and jobs. Spaces are described as the App Store of AI with apps for everything. Jobs are one-off compute tasks paid by duration that end on success or failure. MCP can query remote Spaces: demo generates 'baklava made of yarn' image via Qwen image Space. A 'dynamic spaces' setting (experimental) must be toggled on for full Space access.

sections.title: Case Study: OCR Processing for AI Papers
sections.summary: Colleague Niels built a pipeline to OCR 30,000 AI papers on HF Hub using Codex open OCR models and jobs, all through prompting. Steps: pick an OCR model via OCR-bench (Chandra OCR was first result), ask LLM to write the processing script and kick off the job on HF infra, and the skill handles instance setup without manual napkin math. A new skill recommends best OCR models for fine-tuning including smaller options. Jobs can rerun using HF's new 'buckets' infra product (cheaper and faster than S3) via mounting. Closing links provided to get started.
